drhp.business: The Company manufactures Bearings, Bushings, Thrust Washers, Strips and Alloy Powder, selling through three segments - Original Equipment, After Market and Exports. It supplies OEMs directly and, increasingly for products like bushings, Tier 1 suppliers who are themselves engaged in global business, and has commenced supplies to OEM customers built to the new emission norms. During the year it also entered a new Engineering and Projects segment covering equipment design and manufacture, and proposes to enter the EV business with manufacture and supply of battery pack power systems.

The new powder facility has been in operation for the last two years, and customer development in the sintering, brazing, filter and printing industries has progressed aggressively, with export markets for powders also being pursued. risks.note: The last quarter of the year witnessed high price increases in all inputs - steel, non-ferrous metals, petroleum products and gases - due to the geo-political conflict in the Middle East; availability was also a serious issue which posed challenges in fulfilling commitments to customers, and management states the challenges continue to exist with higher levels of prices and shortages of critical inputs.
risks.risk: Raw material price inflation and shortage of critical inputs

risks.note: Products like bushings have become more for supply into Tier 1 suppliers than to OEMs directly. The AR calls this both an advantage and a disadvantage, and states explicitly that on the negative side there are business risks associated with such opportunities.
risks.risk: Dependence on Tier 1 suppliers rather than direct OEM supply

risks.note: While quality, delivery and price have to be competitive, the AR flags that the important requirement of Global warranty needs to be studied in the background of the warranty clauses provided by the OEMs - a liability tail on parts exported to plants outside the country.
risks.risk: Global warranty exposure in the export / global supply chain

risks.note: Electric motive power in relation to replacement of IC engines has gained traction in the two wheeler, three wheeler and passenger car segments and inter-city EV travel has gained acceptance; the Company notes ICE sales growth relative to EV is still significant and says it will continue investment in its core products albeit cautiously, which frames the pace of the EV shift as the key structural uncertainty.
risks.risk: Electrification of the vehicle fleet eroding the ICE-linked core product base

risks.note: New generations of vehicles conforming to stringent emission norms call for bearings with matching characteristics, and multi-fuel and blended-gasoline options are being explored by OEMs; staying on new platforms depends on continuously pre-positioning materials, coatings and processes.
risks.risk: Technology / emission-norm obsolescence in core products

risks.note: The battery-pack manufacturing facility is still under installation, trials are ongoing and only initial orders for battery packs and BMS have been received, while the Engineering and Projects segment is new and its revenue is recognised stage-wise - so both revenue streams are unproven.
risks.risk: Execution risk in the new EV battery-pack and Engineering and Projects ventures

risks.note: Operations of all core products were consolidated into the Hosur plant last year. The AR presents this as a source of economies of scale and cost control, but it means core output now depends on one site.
risks.risk: Concentration of all core-product manufacturing at a single location

risks.note: The Secretarial Audit Report qualifies its compliance opinion, stating the Company is yet to transfer the shares becoming due for transfer to the demat account of the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority and to file the necessary e-forms; the Directors' Report says the transfer is in process.
risks.risk: Outstanding statutory transfer flagged by the Secretarial Auditor
